newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli hotels had poor 1996, figures show.
newsitem.headline: Israeli hotels had poor 1996, figures show.

text.p: Israel's hotel industry enjoyed a slight increase in dollar revenues last year the industry's association said on Monday, but otherwise it was a gloomy year marked by a wave of suicide bombings that killed 59 people and almost halted the flow of visitors.
Tourist arrivals, including cruise ship passengers, dropped eight percent to 2.3 million in 1996 compared with the previous year, according to the Israel Hotels Association.
Israeli-Palestinian violence that erupted after the government opened a second entrance to a archaelogical tunnel near Moslem holy sites in East Jerusalem last September also scared visitors away.
The association nevertheless said it is optimistic about prospects for 1997.

Industry revenues grew slightly to $1.2 billion in 1996 from $1.16 billion in 1995, with about half the total generated by tourists from abroad, the association said. But measured by the the local currency, revenues were down for the year.
"Because there was no devaluation of the dollar, the figures mark a growth in nominal terms but an erosion in real terms," said spokesman Gilad Nahum.

The average occupancy rate in Israeli tourist class hotels declined to 65.5 percent last year compared with 68.1 percent in 1995, the association said. It said tourists from abroad were spending fewer nights in hotels but that Israeli vacationers were making up for the decline.
"Despite the decline in incoming tourism, we believe that Israel is attractive to the Christian and Jewish tourist markets," said Avraham Rosenthal, the association's director.
"We are starting to see signs of recovery in these markets as the spring and summer approach," he said.
